title: Beautiful Rook Sacs
summary: Keep the pawn alive by offering the rook on squares that turn a king capture into a fork.

nodes.question: How can White keep f7 from being captured?
nodes.explanation: White has Kf1, Rh6 and f7 against Ke7 and Bb7. Rd6 offers the rook and prepares a seventh-rank fork if the king captures f7.

branches.title: The king takes the pawn
commentary: Begin from the complete five-piece source position. The final ...Ke6 retreat and rook capture are independently supplied to complete the source’s fork.
Rd6 offers the rook while preparing Rd7+ if Black takes the pawn.
Kxf7 accepts the pawn, placing king and bishop on the seventh rank.
Rd7+ checks Kf7 while attacking Bb7.
Ke6 is an independently selected legal reply to complete the illustrated fork idea.
Rxb7 captures the bishop. Rook versus bare king is exactly won.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Rxb7 captures the bishop. Rook versus bare king is exactly won.

branches.title: The bishop retreats to a8
commentary: Compare the source’s bishop retreat that keeps an eye on promotion.
Rd6 prepares the rook’s lateral checking tactics.
Ba8 retreats to the corner.
f8=Q+ offers the promoted queen with check.
Kxf8 takes the queen, placing king and bishop on the eighth rank.
Rd8+ checks and attacks Ba8 along the same rank. The exact position is winning; the line stops at the checked fork.
branches.explanation: Rd8+ checks and attacks Ba8 along the same rank. The exact position is winning; the line stops at the checked fork.

branches.title: The bishop retreats to e4
commentary: Compare the source’s central bishop retreat.
Rd6 offers the same pawn-protecting rook sacrifice.
Be4 moves the bishop to a central diagonal.
Re6+ checks the king while placing the rook on the bishop’s file.
Kxf7 takes the pawn but leaves Be4 to the rook.
Rxe4 captures the bishop. The exact rook-versus-king ending is won.
branches.explanation: Rxe4 captures the bishop. The exact rook-versus-king ending is won.

branches.title: Defend from h8 instead
commentary: Compare the source’s tempting rook retreat before the fork has been prepared.
Rh8 gives up the exact win by allowing a bishop check that removes the defender from the seventh rank.
Ba6+ checks Kf1 and moves the bishop away from a future seventh-rank fork.
Kf2 answers the illustrated check.
Kxf7 removes the pawn. The exact rook-versus-bishop ending is drawn here.
branches.explanation: Kxf7 removes the pawn. The exact rook-versus-bishop ending is drawn here.

exercises.prompt: Why does Rd6 protect a pawn it does not directly defend?
exercises.answer: If the king takes f7, Rd7+ attacks king and bishop on the same rank. The tactical threat protects the pawn indirectly.

exercises.prompt: Why does the bishop check matter after Rh8?
exercises.answer: ...Ba6+ forces a king response and removes the bishop from the seventh rank, so ...Kxf7 no longer permits the same fork.

startContext: The complete five-piece source root is visually reconstructed. Selected source branches use Rd6, bishop retreats and promoted-queen sacrifices to make rook forks possible. The ...Ke6/Rxb7 completion of the first fork is independently supplied and labeled. Every encoded position is checked; the won forks are not presented as completed mates.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
